---
name: Mongo index name compatibility
description: Production index names can differ from Mongo-generated names despite identical key patterns.
---

Do not infer a production Mongo index's name from its key pattern. Prefer a key-pattern hint where equivalent-index ambiguity is not a concern, or inspect the deployed index catalog first.

**Why:** A production relay-monitor read failed with Mongo BadValue because it forced an autogenerated index name while the same compound index existed under a custom name. The identical bounded query using the actual name succeeded; this was an observability failure, not missing transport data or a need for another index.

**How to apply:** For hinted readers, distinguish missing indexes from naming mismatches using read-only catalog inspection in the approved production runtime. Preserve query limits and deadlines; do not remove hints and allow broad scans merely to hide the error.

A Mongo index command interrupted by a replica-state change does not prove the
index failed to build.

**Why:** A production create-index command returned code 11602, but catalog
inspection, an explicitly hinted read, and a subsequent unhinted query confirmed
the index existed and was usable. Reissuing DDL immediately would have confused
the operation's outcome.

**How to apply:** Check the live catalog and active index-build operations before
retrying. Verify actual query-plan selection and examined-document counts; use
the application query shape rather than assuming every projection gets the same
plan. Keep client-command success separate from server-side completion.
